sanskrit: mahī viyad dyauḥ salilāni vāyunā; yathā vibhinnāni vibhānti bhārata tathaiva śabdo bhuvaneṣv abhūt tadā; janā vyavasyan vyathitāś ca caskhaluḥ
english: As earth, mid-air, the heavens, and the waters appear riven asunder by the wind, O Bhārata, even so did that sound arise then throughout the worlds; men reeled in dismay and lost their footing.

sanskrit: tataḥ samudgrathya sitena vāsasā; svamūrdhajānavyathitaḥ sthito 'rjunaḥ vibhāti saṃpūrṇamarīcibhāsvatā; śirogatenodayaparvato yathā
english: Then, binding up his hair with a strip of white cloth, Arjuna stood unshaken, and shone like the mountain of sunrise crowned with the full-rayed, radiant sun upon its summit.

sanskrit: balāhakaḥ karṇabhujeritas tato; hutāśanārkapratimadyutir mahān mahoragaḥ kṛtavairo 'rjunena; kirīṭam āsādya samutpapāta
english: Then the great cloud-like shaft, sped by Karṇa's arm, blazing like fire and sun—the mighty serpent who bore an old feud with Arjuna—reaching the diademed one's crown, sprang forth.

sanskrit: tam abravīd viddhi kṛtāgasaṃ me; kṛṣṇādya mātur vadhajātavairam tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pārtham uvāca saṃkhye; mahoragaṃ kṛtavairaṃ jahi tvam
english: Kṛṣṇa said, "Know him, this one who has wronged me, whose enmity was born of his mother's slaying." Then Kṛṣṇa said to Pārtha in the battle, "Slay you this great serpent who bears the ancient feud."

sanskrit: sa evam ukto madhusūdanena; gāṇḍīvadhanvā ripuṣūgradhanvā uvāca ko nv eṣa mamādya nāgaḥ; svayaṃ ya āgād garuḍasya vaktram
english: Thus addressed by the slayer of Madhu, the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, fierce-bowed among foes, said, "Who indeed is this serpent of mine today, who has come of his own accord into the mouth of Garuḍa?"

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca yo 'sau tvayā khāṇḍave citrabhānuṃ; saṃtarpayānena dhanurdhareṇa viyadgato bāṇanikṛttadeho; hy anekarūpo nihatāsya mātā
english: Kṛṣṇa said, "He whom you, the bowman who sated the fire-god in Khāṇḍava, drove into the sky—his body severed by your arrows, taking many shapes—his mother it was you slew."

sanskrit: tatas tu jiṣṇuḥ parihṛtya śeṣāṃś; ciccheda ṣaḍbhir niśitaiḥ sudhāraiḥ nāgaṃ viyat tiryag ivotpatantaṃ; sa chinnagātro nipapāta bhūmau
english: Then the victorious one, turning aside the rest, cut with six keen and well-edged shafts the serpent that flew slantwise across the sky; and with severed body it fell to the earth.

sanskrit: tasmin muhūrte daśabhiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ; śilāśitair barhiṇavājitaiś ca vivyādha karṇaḥ puruṣapravīraṃ; dhanaṃjayaṃ tiryag avekṣamāṇam
english: In that very instant, with ten arrows whetted on stone and fledged with peacock feathers, Karṇa pierced Dhanaṃjaya, foremost of men, as he gazed askance.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno dvādaśabhir vimuktair; ākarṇamuktair niśitaiḥ samarpya nārācam āśīviṣatulyavegam; ākarṇapūrṇāyatam utsasarja
english: Then Arjuna, having let fly twelve keen shafts drawn back to the ear, loosed an iron dart swift as a venomous snake, drawn full to the ear.

sanskrit: sa citravarmeṣuvaro vidārya; prāṇān nirasyann iva sādhu muktaḥ karṇasya pītvā rudhiraṃ viveśa; vasuṃdharāṃ śoṇitavājadigdhaḥ
english: That choicest of shafts, well loosed, rending his bright armor as though tearing out his life, drank Karṇa's blood and entered the earth, its feathers smeared with gore.

sanskrit: tato vṛṣo bāṇanipātakopito; mahorago daṇḍavighaṭṭito yathā tathāśukārī vyasṛjac charottamān; mahāviṣaḥ sarpa ivottamaṃ viṣam
english: Then the Bull-like one, enraged by the fall of that arrow, like a great serpent struck with a staff, swift in act, loosed his choicest shafts as a deadly snake spews its uttermost venom.

sanskrit: janārdanaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ parābhinan; navair navatyā ca śarais tathārjunam śareṇa ghoreṇa punaś ca pāṇḍavaṃ; vibhidya karṇo 'bhyanadaj jahāsa ca
english: He smote Janārdana with twelve fresh shafts, and Arjuna with ninety; and piercing the Pāṇḍava once more with a dreadful arrow, Karṇa roared aloud and laughed.

sanskrit: tam asya harṣaṃ mamṛṣe na pāṇḍavo; bibheda marmāṇi tato 'sya marmavit paraṃ śaraiḥ patribhir indravikramas; tathā yathendro balam ojasāhanat
english: The Pāṇḍava brooked not this exultation of his; knowing the vital points, he pierced his foe's vitals with feathered shafts, valiant as Indra, as Indra with his might struck down Bala.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarāṇāṃ navatīr navārjunaḥ; sasarja karṇe 'ntakadaṇḍasaṃnibhāḥ śarair bhṛśāyastatanuḥ pravivyathe; tathā yathā vajravidārito 'calaḥ
english: Then Arjuna loosed at Karṇa ninety-nine arrows like the rod of Death; and Karṇa, his body sorely racked by those shafts, trembled like a mountain riven by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: maṇipravekottamavajrahāṭakair; alaṃkṛtaṃ cāsya varāṅgabhūṣaṇam praviddham urvyāṃ nipapāta patribhir; dhanaṃjayenottamakuṇḍale 'pi ca
english: His fair ornament, adorned with choice gems, the finest diamonds and gold, struck off by the feathered shafts of Dhanaṃjaya, fell to the earth, and his splendid earrings as well.

sanskrit: mahādhanaṃ śilpivaraiḥ prayatnataḥ; kṛtaṃ yad asyottamavarma bhāsvaram sudīrghakālena tad asya pāṇḍavaḥ; kṣaṇena bāṇair bahudhā vyaśātayat
english: That priceless, gleaming armor of his, wrought with toil over long ages by the best of craftsmen, the Pāṇḍava shattered in a moment, breaking it in many places with his arrows.

sanskrit: sa taṃ vivarmāṇam athottameṣubhiḥ; śaraiś caturbhiḥ kupitaḥ parābhinat sa vivyathe 'tyartham ariprahārito; yathāturaḥ pittakaphānilavraṇaiḥ
english: Then, in wrath, he smote that armorless one with four of his finest shafts; and stricken by his foe, he writhed exceedingly, like a sick man afflicted by ailments of bile, phlegm, and wind.

sanskrit: mahādhanurmaṇḍalaniḥsṛtaiḥ śitaiḥ; kriyāprayatnaprahitair balena ca tatakṣa karṇaṃ bahubhiḥ śarottamair; bibheda marmasv api cārjunas tvaran
english: With keen shafts sped from the circle of his great bow, hurled with skill, effort, and strength, Arjuna in haste hewed Karṇa with many a choice arrow and pierced him even in his vital parts.

sanskrit: dṛḍhāhataḥ patribhir ugravegaiḥ; pārthena karṇo vividhaiḥ śitāgraiḥ babhau girir gairikadhāturaktaḥ; kṣaran prapātair iva raktam ambhaḥ
english: Struck hard by Pārtha with various keen-pointed, swift-flying shafts, Karṇa shone like a mountain red with ochre ore, streaming red water down its cascades.

sanskrit: sāśvaṃ tu karṇaṃ sarathaṃ kirīṭī; samācinod bhārata vatsadantaiḥ pracchādayām āsa diśaś ca bāṇaiḥ; sarvaprayatnāt tapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ
english: The diademed one covered Karṇa, with his horses and his chariot, with calf-tooth shafts, O Bhārata, and overspread the very quarters with arrows golden-feathered, sped with all his might.

sanskrit: sa vatsadantaiḥ pṛthupīnavakṣāḥ; samācitaḥ smādhirathir vibhāti supuṣpitāśokapalāśaśālmalir; yathācalaḥ spandanacandanāyutaḥ
english: That son of Adhiratha, broad and full of chest, studded with calf-tooth shafts, shone like a mountain decked with aśoka and palāśa and śālmali trees in full bloom, and with spandana and sandalwood.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ śarīre bahudhā samarpitair; vibhāti karṇaḥ samare viśāṃ pate mahīruhair ācitasānukandaro; yathā mahendraḥ śubhakarṇikāravān
english: With arrows lodged in his body in many places, Karṇa shone in the battle, O lord of peoples, like the great mountain Mahendra, its slopes and caverns thick with trees and lovely with karṇikāra blossoms.

sanskrit: sa bāṇasaṃghān dhanuṣā vyavāsṛjan; vibhāti karṇaḥ śarajālaraśmivān salohito raktagabhastimaṇḍalo; divākaro 'stābhimukho yathā tathā
english: Loosing volleys of arrows from his bow, Karṇa shone, rayed with his net of shafts, blood-reddened, his orb of red beams—like the day-maker turned toward his setting.

sanskrit: bāhvantarād ādhirather vimuktān; bāṇān mahāhīn iva dīpyamānān vyadhvaṃsayann arjunabāhumuktāḥ; śarāḥ samāsādya diśaḥ śitāgrāḥ
english: The arrows loosed from between the arms of Adhiratha's son, blazing like great serpents, the keen-pointed shafts sped from Arjuna's arms met and scattered to the quarters.

sanskrit: tataś cakramapatat tasya bhūmau; sa vihvalaḥ samare sūtaputraḥ ghūrṇe rathe brāhmaṇasyābhiśāpād; rāmād upātte 'pratibhāti cāstre
english: Then his chariot-wheel sank into the earth, and the charioteer's son was bewildered in the battle; his car lurched by the brāhmaṇa's curse, and the weapon learned from Rāma would not come to his mind.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇo vyasanāni tāni; hastau vidhunvan sa vigarhamāṇaḥ dharmapradhānān abhipāti dharma; ity abruvan dharmavidaḥ sadaiva mamāpi nimno 'dya na pāti bhaktān; manye na nityaṃ paripāti dharmaḥ
english: Unable to bear these calamities, wringing his hands, he reviled it: "Knowers of dharma have ever said that dharma guards those devoted to dharma; yet today, though I am bowed before it, it guards not its votaries—I think dharma does not always protect."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvan praskhalitāśvasūto; vicālyamāno 'rjunaśastrapātaiḥ marmābhighātāc calitaḥ kriyāsu; punaḥ punar dharmam agarhad ājau
english: Thus speaking, his horses and driver staggering, shaken by the fall of Arjuna's weapons, faltering in his deeds from the blows upon his vitals, again and again he reviled dharma in the fight.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarair bhīmatarair avidhyat tribhir āhave haste karṇas tadā pārtham abhyavidhyac ca saptabhiḥ
english: Then Karṇa pierced Pārtha's hand in the battle with three most dreadful shafts, and struck him besides with seven.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ saptadaśa tigmatejān ajihmagān indrāśanisamān ghorān asṛjat pāvakopamān
english: Then Arjuna loosed seventeen fierce-flaming arrows, straight-flying, dreadful, like Indra's bolt and like fire itself.

sanskrit: nirbhidya te bhīmavegā nyapatan pṛthivītale kampitātmā tathā karṇaḥ śaktyā ceṣṭām adarśayat
english: Those shafts of terrible speed pierced him through and fell upon the ground; and Karṇa, shaken to his soul, yet by sheer strength kept up his exertions.

sanskrit: balenātha sa saṃstabhya brahmāstraṃ samudairayat aindrāstram arjunaś cāpi tad dṛṣṭvābhinyamantrayat
english: Then, steadying himself by force, he sent forth the Brahmā weapon; and Arjuna, seeing it, invoked the weapon of Indra in answer.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvaṃ jyāṃ ca bāṇāṃś ca anumantrya dhanaṃjayaḥ asṛjac charavarṣāṇi varṣāṇīva puraṃdaraḥ
english: Charging Gāṇḍīva, the string, and the arrows with sacred spells, Dhanaṃjaya loosed showers of shafts, as Purandara pours down his rains.

sanskrit: tatas tejomayā bāṇā rathāt pārthasya niḥsṛtāḥ prādurāsan mahāvīryāḥ karṇasya ratham antikāt
english: Then arrows full of splendor, issuing from Pārtha's car, appeared, full of great might, close beside Karṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: tān karṇas tv agrato 'bhyastān moghāṃś cakre mahārathaḥ tato 'bravīd vṛṣṇivīras tasminn astre vināśite
english: But Karṇa, the great car-warrior, made those shafts that sped before him fall in vain; and when that weapon was undone, the hero of the Vṛṣṇis spoke.

sanskrit: visṛjāstraṃ paraṃ pārtha rādheyo grasate śarān brahmāstram arjunaś cāpi saṃmantryātha prayojayat
english: "Loose your supreme weapon, Pārtha—Rādheya devours your shafts." And Arjuna, having charged it with spells, then sent forth the Brahmā weapon.

sanskrit: chādayitvā tato bāṇaiḥ karṇaṃ prabhrāmya cārjunaḥ tasya karṇaḥ śaraiḥ kruddhaś ciccheda jyāṃ sutejanaiḥ
english: Then, covering Karṇa with arrows and wheeling about, Arjuna pressed him; but Karṇa, in wrath, cut his bowstring with keen, well-tempered shafts.

sanskrit: tato jyām avadhāyānyām anumṛjya ca pāṇḍavaḥ śarair avākirat karṇaṃ dīpyamānaiḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Then, fastening another string and drawing his hand along it, the Pāṇḍava overwhelmed Karṇa with blazing arrows by the thousand.

sanskrit: tasya jyācchedanaṃ karṇo jyāvadhānaṃ ca saṃyuge nānvabudhyata śīghratvāt tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: So swift was he that Karṇa, in the battle, did not even perceive the cutting of the string nor the fixing of the new—and this was as though a marvel.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi rādheyaḥ pratyahan savyasācinaḥ cakre cābhyadhikaṃ pārthāt svavīryaṃ pratidarśayan
english: Rādheya struck down weapon with weapon against the ambidextrous archer, and displayed his own prowess as surpassing even Pārtha's.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇo 'rjunaṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇāstreṇābhipīḍitam abhyasyety abravīt pārtham ātiṣṭhāstram anuttamam
english: Then Kṛṣṇa, seeing Arjuna hard pressed by Karṇa's weapon, said to Pārtha, "Strike! Bring to bear your peerless weapon."

sanskrit: tato 'nyam agnisadṛśaṃ śaraṃ sarpaviṣopamam aśmasāramayaṃ divyam anumantrya dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya charged with spells another arrow, like fire, like serpent's venom, made of tempered steel, and divine.

sanskrit: raudram astraṃ samādāya kṣeptukāmaḥ kirīṭavān tato 'grasan mahī cakraṃ rādheyasya mahāmṛdhe
english: And as the diademed one took up the dread weapon, eager to hurl it, in that great battle the earth swallowed Rādheya's chariot-wheel.

sanskrit: grastacakras tu rādheyaḥ kopād aśrūṇy avartayat so 'bravīd arjunaṃ cāpi muhūrtaṃ kṣama pāṇḍava
english: With his wheel devoured, Rādheya in his anguish let fall tears, and he said to Arjuna, "Forbear a moment, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: madhye cakram avagrastaṃ dṛṣṭvā daivād idaṃ mama pārtha kāpuruṣācīrṇam abhisaṃdhiṃ vivarjaya
english: "Seeing my wheel here swallowed by fate, Pārtha, forsake the resolve that befits only a coward.

sanskrit: prakīrṇakeśe vimukhe brāhmaṇe ca kṛtāñjalau śaraṇāgate nyastaśastre tathā vyasanage 'rjuna
english: Upon one whose hair is loosened, who turns away, upon a brāhmaṇa with joined palms, upon one who has come for refuge, who has laid down his arms, or who is fallen into distress, O Arjuna—

sanskrit: abāṇe bhraṣṭakavace bhraṣṭabhagnāyudhe tathā na śūrāḥ praharanty ājau na rājñe pārthivās tathā tvaṃ ca śūro 'si kaunteya tasmāt kṣama muhūrtakam
english: upon one without an arrow, his armor fallen, his weapon slipped or broken—heroes strike not in battle, nor do princes so deal with a king. You too are a hero, son of Kuntī; therefore forbear a moment.

sanskrit: yāvac cakram idaṃ bhūmer uddharāmi dhanaṃjaya na māṃ rathastho bhūmiṣṭham asajjaṃ hantum arhasi na vāsudevāt tvatto vā pāṇḍaveya bibhemy aham
english: Until I lift this wheel from the earth, Dhanaṃjaya, you, standing in your car, ought not to slay me who am on the ground and unready. Not of Vāsudeva, nor of you, son of Pāṇḍu, am I afraid.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi kṣatriyadāyādo mahākulavivardhanaḥ smṛtvā dharmopadeśaṃ tvaṃ muhūrtaṃ kṣama pāṇḍava
english: You are an heir of the kṣatriya line, the increaser of a great house. Remembering the teaching of dharma, forbear a moment, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca athābravīd vāsudevo rathastho; rādheya diṣṭyā smarasīha dharmam prāyeṇa nīcā vyasaneṣu magnā; nindanti daivaṃ kukṛtaṃ na tat tat
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Vāsudeva, standing in the car, spoke: "Rādheya, how fortunate that you remember dharma now! Commonly the base, when sunk in calamity, blame fate—but not their own ill deeds, never those."

sanskrit: yad draupadīm ekavastrāṃ sabhāyām; ānāyya tvaṃ caiva suyodhanaś ca duḥśāsanaḥ śakuniḥ saubalaś ca; na te karṇa pratyabhāt tatra dharmaḥ
english: "When Draupadī, clad in a single garment, was haled into the hall—you, and Suyodhana, and Duḥśāsana, and Śakuni son of Subala—then, Karṇa, dharma did not shine forth for you there.

sanskrit: yadā sabhāyāṃ kaunteyam anakṣajñaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram akṣajñaḥ śakunir jetā tadā dharmaḥ kva te gataḥ
english: When in the hall Śakuni, skilled at the dice, defeated the son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira who knew not the dice—where then had your dharma gone?

sanskrit: yadā rajasvalāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ duḥśāsanavaśe sthitām sabhāyāṃ prāhasaḥ karṇa kva te dharmas tadā gataḥ
english: When Kṛṣṇā, in her courses, stood in Duḥśāsana's power, and you laughed aloud in the hall, Karṇa—where then had your dharma gone?

sanskrit: rājyalubdhaḥ punaḥ karṇa samāhvayasi pāṇḍavam gāndhārarājam āśritya kva te dharmas tadā gataḥ
english: Greedy for the kingdom, Karṇa, leaning on the king of Gāndhāra, you summoned the Pāṇḍava again—where then had your dharma gone?"

sanskrit: evam ukte tu rādheye vāsudevena pāṇḍavam manyur abhyāviśat tīvraḥ smṛtvā tat tad dhanaṃjayam
english: When Rādheya had thus been addressed by Vāsudeva, a fierce wrath entered the Pāṇḍava, as Dhanaṃjaya called to mind each of those deeds.

sanskrit: tasya krodhena sarvebhyaḥ srotobhyas tejaso 'rciṣaḥ prādurāsan mahārāja tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: From his wrath, O great king, flames of splendor sprang forth from every pore of his body; and that was as though a marvel.

sanskrit: taṃ samīkṣya tataḥ karṇo brahmāstreṇa dhanaṃjayam abhyavarṣat punar yatnam akarod rathasarjane tad astram astreṇāvārya prajahārāsya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Seeing this, Karṇa then rained upon Dhanaṃjaya with the Brahmā weapon and strove anew to free his chariot. Warding off that weapon with a weapon, the Pāṇḍava struck at him.

sanskrit: tato 'nyad astraṃ kaunteyo dayitaṃ jātavedasaḥ mumoca karṇam uddiśya tat prajajvāla vai bhṛśam
english: Then the son of Kuntī loosed another weapon, the cherished one of the fire-god, aimed at Karṇa; and it blazed up fiercely.

sanskrit: vāruṇena tataḥ karṇaḥ śamayām āsa pāvakam jīmūtaiś ca diśaḥ sarvāś cakre timiradurdināḥ
english: With the weapon of Varuṇa Karṇa then quenched that fire, and with masses of cloud made all the quarters dark and overcast.

sanskrit: pāṇḍaveyas tv asaṃbhrānto vāyavyāstreṇa vīryavān apovāha tadābhrāṇi rādheyasya prapaśyataḥ
english: But the valiant son of Pāṇḍu, unperturbed, with the weapon of Vāyu drove away those clouds while Rādheya looked on.

sanskrit: taṃ hastikakṣyāpravaraṃ ca bāṇaiḥ; suvarṇamuktāmaṇivajramṛṣṭam kālaprayatnottamaśilpiyatnaiḥ; kṛtaṃ surūpaṃ vitamaskam uccaiḥ
english: That foremost standard—bright with the elephant-girth emblem, burnished with gold and pearls and gems and diamonds, fashioned fair and lofty and unclouded by the labor over long time of the most skillful of craftsmen—

sanskrit: ūrjaskaraṃ tava sainyasya nityam; amitravitrāsanam īḍyarūpam vikhyātam ādityasamasya loke; tviṣā samaṃ pāvakabhānucandraiḥ
english: ever giving strength to your host, terrifying to foes, of praiseworthy form, renowned throughout the world as belonging to one equal to the sun, in radiance like fire, sun, and moon—

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣureṇādhiratheḥ kirīṭī; suvarṇapuṅkhena śitena yattaḥ śriyā jvalantaṃ dhvajam unmamātha; mahārathasyādhirather mahātmā
english: with a keen, gold-feathered razor-shaft, intent, the great-souled diademed one tore down the banner of Adhiratha's son, that great car-warrior—the standard ablaze with splendor.

sanskrit: yaśaś ca dharmaś ca jayaś ca māriṣa; priyāṇi sarvāṇi ca tena ketunā tadā kurūṇāṃ hṛdayāni cāpatan; babhūva hāheti ca nisvano mahān
english: With that banner, O sir, glory and dharma and victory and all things dear fell away, and with it the hearts of the Kurus sank; and a great cry of "Alas, alas!" arose.

sanskrit: atha tvaran karṇavadhāya pāṇḍavo; mahendravajrānaladaṇḍasaṃnibham ādatta pārtho 'ñjalikaṃ niṣaṅgāt; sahasraraśmer iva raśmim uttamam
english: Then, hastening to slay Karṇa, Pārtha the Pāṇḍava took from his quiver the añjalika shaft, like the thunderbolt of great Indra, like the rod of fire, like the supreme ray of the thousand-rayed sun—

sanskrit: marmacchidaṃ śoṇitamāṃsadigdhaṃ; vaiśvānarārkapratimaṃ mahārham narāśvanāgāsuharaṃ tryaratniṃ; ṣaḍvājam añjogatim ugravegam
english: piercer of vitals, smeared with blood and flesh, like fire and sun, of priceless worth, slayer of the lives of men and horses and elephants, three cubits long, six-feathered, straight in flight, of terrible speed—

sanskrit: sahasranetrāśanitulyatejasaṃ; samānakravyādam ivātiduḥsaham pinākanārāyaṇacakrasaṃnibhaṃ; bhayaṃkaraṃ prāṇabhṛtāṃ vināśanam
english: equal in splendor to the bolt of the thousand-eyed god, hard to bear as a flesh-devouring fiend, like Pināka and Nārāyaṇa's discus, terrible, the destroyer of all that breathes.

sanskrit: yuktvā mahāstreṇa pareṇa mantravid; vikṛṣya gāṇḍīvam uvāca sasvanam ayaṃ mahāstro 'pratimo dhṛtaḥ śaraḥ; śarīrabhic cāsuharaś ca durhṛdaḥ
english: Joining it to a supreme great weapon, the knower of spells drew Gāṇḍīva and said aloud: "This great, matchless arrow is fixed, the breaker of bodies and the taker of life from the malign foe.

sanskrit: tapo 'sti taptaṃ guravaś ca toṣitā; mayā yad iṣṭaṃ suhṛdāṃ tathā śrutam anena satyena nihantv ayaṃ śaraḥ; sudaṃśitaḥ karṇam ariṃ mamājitaḥ
english: If austerity I have performed, and my elders satisfied, and the welfare of my friends desired by me, and sacred lore heard—by that truth let this well-aimed and unfailing shaft slay Karṇa, my enemy."

sanskrit: ity ūcivāṃs taṃ sa mumoca bāṇaṃ; dhanaṃjayaḥ karṇavadhāya ghoram kṛtyām atharvāṅgirasīm ivogrāṃ; dīptām asahyāṃ yudhi mṛtyunāpi
english: Having so spoken, Dhanaṃjaya loosed that dreadful arrow for the slaying of Karṇa—fierce as a spell of the Atharva-Aṅgiras, blazing, unbearable in battle even to Death himself.

sanskrit: bruvan kirīṭī tam atiprahṛṣṭo; ayaṃ śaro me vijayāvaho 'stu jighāṃsur arkendusamaprabhāvaḥ; karṇaṃ samāptiṃ nayatāṃ yamāya
english: The diademed one, exceedingly glad, said as he loosed it: "May this arrow of mine bring me victory; let it, of power equal to sun and moon, bear Karṇa to his end and to Yama."

sanskrit: teneṣuvaryeṇa kirīṭamālī; prahṛṣṭarūpo vijayāvahena jighāṃsur arkendusamaprabheṇa; cakre viṣaktaṃ ripum ātatāyī
english: With that choicest of shafts, victory-bringing, of splendor equal to sun and moon, the diademed and garlanded one, glad of aspect, the drawn-bow warrior bent on slaying, transfixed his foe.

sanskrit: tad udyatādityasamānavarcasaṃ; śarannabhomadhyagabhāskaropamam varāṅgam urvyām apatac camūpater; divākaro 'stād iva raktamaṇḍalaḥ
english: That fair head of the army's lord, of splendor like the risen sun, like the sun at the midpoint of the autumn sky, fell to the earth, like the day-maker with his red orb sinking from the firmament.

sanskrit: tad asya dehī satataṃ sukhoditaṃ; svarūpam atyartham udārakarmaṇaḥ pareṇa kṛcchreṇa śarīram atyajad; gṛhaṃ maharddhīva sasaṅgam īśvaraḥ
english: With utmost reluctance the indweller forsook the body of that ever-blessed, exceedingly fair-formed doer of noble deeds—as a lord, attached to it, leaves a house of great abundance.

sanskrit: śarair vibhugnaṃ vyasu tad vivarmaṇaḥ; papāta karṇasya śarīram ucchritam sravadvraṇaṃ gairikatoyavisravaṃ; girer yathā vajrahataṃ śiras tathā
english: Broken by arrows, lifeless and stripped of armor, the towering body of Karṇa fell, its wounds streaming like a flow of ochre-tinted water, as the thunder-smitten summit of a mountain falls.

sanskrit: dehāt tu karṇasya nipātitasya; tejo dīptaṃ khaṃ vigāhyācireṇa tad adbhutaṃ sarvamanuṣyayodhāḥ; paśyanti rājan nihate sma karṇe
english: From the body of the fallen Karṇa a blazing splendor swiftly rose and plunged into the sky; and all the warriors among men beheld that marvel, O king, when Karṇa was slain.

sanskrit: taṃ somakāḥ prekṣya hataṃ śayānaṃ; prītā nādaṃ saha sainyair akurvan tūryāṇi cājaghnur atīva hṛṣṭā; vāsāṃsi caivādudhuvur bhujāṃś ca balānvitāś cāpy apare hy anṛtyann; anyonyam āśliṣya nadanta ūcuḥ
english: The Somakas, beholding him slain and lying low, raised in joy a shout together with their hosts, and overjoyed they beat their drums, and waved their garments and their arms; and others, full of strength, danced, embracing one another, and cried aloud as they spoke.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu karṇaṃ bhuvi niṣṭanantaṃ; hataṃ rathāt sāyakenāvabhinnam mahānilenāgnim ivāpaviddhaṃ; yajñāvasāne śayane niśānte
english: They saw Karṇa moaning upon the ground, slain, struck down from his car by the arrow, like a fire flung down by a great wind—like the laying down of the sacred fire at the close of the rite, at the ending of the night—

sanskrit: śarair ācitasarvāṅgaḥ śoṇitaughapariplutaḥ vibhāti dehaḥ karṇasya svaraśmibhir ivāṃśumān
english: his every limb thick-set with arrows, deluged in floods of blood, the body of Karṇa shone like the sun amid its own rays.

sanskrit: pratāpya senām āmitrīṃ dīptaiḥ śaragabhastibhiḥ balinārjunakālena nīto 'staṃ karṇabhāskaraḥ
english: Having scorched the hostile host with the blazing beams of his arrows, the sun that was Karṇa was brought to its setting by the mighty Arjuna acting as Time.

sanskrit: astaṃ gacchan yathādityaḥ prabhām ādāya gacchati evaṃ jīvitam ādāya karṇasyeṣur jagāma ha
english: As the sun, going to its setting, departs taking the light with it, so the arrow departed, bearing away the life of Karṇa.
